source.title: Rethinking Model Selection in VLM Through the Lens of Gromov-Wasserstein Distance
source.authors: Mu-Yang Li; Yuchen Liu; Jian-Bo Ma; E. Osborne; Bo Han; Tong-Liang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study compares cross-modal representation-similarity measures and their association with downstream VLM performance, using GW rather than the original MutualNN approach. It does not test convergence as model scale increases.
record.gate_note: The reported GW, RSA, CCA, and MutualNN correlations in Table 5 bear on cross-modal similarity and metric dependence. The model-selection tables report downstream performance for models selected by each method, not alignment measurements, so those results are not separate alignment rows. The study does not sweep model scale or report alignment trends as both models become more capable.
record.test_reason: The study uses cross-modal similarity measures (GW, RSA, CCA, MutualNN) between vision-encoder and LLM features as selection tools. It reports how well each predicts downstream VLM performance after training. It never reports how alignment changes as either model becomes larger or more capable: the LLM is fixed per analysis and no alignment-vs-encoder-size or alignment-vs-encoder-accuracy result is given. Table 5 measures each selection metric's predictive validity, so it does not show whether representations converge. The finding belongs under fits_no_version, not V2 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that GW distance between vision and LLM text representations is an effective training-free predictor of which vision encoder yields a stronger VLM. It outperforms size, zero-shot accuracy, RSA, CCA and MutualNN. The record should add that the authors find MutualNN's correlation negative, opposite to the direction PRH implies, and call it likely spurious. They also claim, with a Lipschitz bound, that smaller GW implies an easier-to-learn cross-modal mapping.
record.recipe_differences: This is a model-selection study using GW distance and comparing it with MutualNN, RSA, and CCA; it is not a replication of the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis measurement or its scaling claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares different similarity metrics and evaluates selections with two base LLMs and a changed pre-training dataset. It reports that GW's selection effectiveness is not significantly affected by the dataset change and that encoder-performance rankings are quite consistent across the two LLMs. It does not systematically vary GW settings or inputs to test convergence sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: With Qwen-2.5-7B and 14 vision encoders, GW distance between image and caption features predicts final VLM performance (|r| 0.66, R2 0.43). MutualNN shows |r| 0.61 but |ρ| 0.18, with the sign opposite to that expected. CCA is near zero. Vision-encoder size and zero-shot accuracy correlate only weakly with VLM performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-training structural similarity between a vision encoder's and an LLM's representations of paired image-text data predicts how well they combine into a VLM. The PRH mutual-NN alignment score does not predict this in the expected direction.

fits_no_version.finding: GW and MutualNN disagree on which large vision encoder is most aligned with Qwen's text features: MutualNN picks DFN5B-ViT-H-378, GW picks SigLIP-SO400M.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different cross-modal alignment measures rank encoder-LLM pairs differently. This touches V6 but is shown only through which model each selects.

record.problems: The correlation analysis is restricted to 14 vision encoders and one base LLM. Table 5 reports absolute correlation values, obscuring direction there; the text separately flags MutualNN's negative direction. The study does not test alignment trends across scale or directly establish that both models become more capable as alignment increases.
record.rows_left_out: Sections 5.2 and 5.3, Tables 1–4 and 6–7 report downstream scores for models selected by each method, not the alignment measurements themselves; these are excluded as rows. No per-encoder GW distances or scale-sweep alignment results are reported.

untested.parts: No measure of alignment across model scale or capability.
No report of image-text alignment as a function of vision-encoder or LLM size or capability. Per-encoder alignment scores are not given.
No measurement of mapping or stitching loss. The MLP projector is trained, but no transfer-loss result is reported.
No variation of k, inputs or OOD data on measured alignment. Metrics are compared only on predicting downstream performance.
No analysis of plateau or of shared-data causes.

missing.what: Per-encoder alignment scores (GW, MutualNN, RSA, CCA) against encoder size and zero-shot accuracy. These are needed to judge V2/V6 directly but are not reported.
missing.locator: Section 5.2 / Figure 1 (only GW vs VLM performance plotted)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V2 and V6 supports is overreach. The study is a model-selection paper whose correlations are with downstream VLM performance after joint fine-tuning, not with model competence. The LLM is fixed within the correlation analysis and only 14 encoders are used, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether representations of independently trained models become more aligned as model size or capability increases.
Tests cross-modal similarity against downstream VLM performance for varying vision encoders, but not whether alignment rises as both the vision and language models improve or scale.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
No test of mapping one model's representations to another's, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Compares similarity metrics, but does not vary similarity settings such as neighbor count or systematically test input choices or out-of-distribution data for convergence.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete.

rows.subject: 14 vision encoders (aggregate; Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct base LLM)
rows.operation_detail: Correlated GW distance with final VLM performance across 14 vision encoders.
rows.measure: Absolute Pearson correlation |r|, absolute Spearman correlation |ρ|, and R-squared between GW distance and final VLM performance
rows.note: The reported correlations are absolute, so this row does not establish their direction. The authors state that GW is the only metric with both correlation magnitudes above 0.5 and that its linear fit explains 43% of variance.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (GW) correlated with downstream VLM performance after LLaVA training, not alignment versus model capability. It cannot show whether alignment rises with scale or competence (V2), or how measured convergence depends on the metric (V6). The values are absolute; GW is a distance, so the expected sign is negative.
